A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MPO/meta-learning study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched across reformatting, renumbering, and relocation, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original TLA and Hopper simulations in Tables 2 and 4 and an LLM alignment experiment in Table 3.

after.justification: v3 retains original MuJoCo results and reports expanded LLM experiments and ablations in Tables 2–3, alongside additional TLA comparisons.

M1.justification: v2's CoLPO gates a clipped linear preference term using chosen-response log-probability. v3 replaces it with TA-MPO, which gradually shifts weight from SFT to preference optimization during training. Sections 3 and 4.3 introduce its objective and SimPO-based instantiation with linear, quadratic, and sigmoid schedules. This changes the training procedure substantially.

E1.justification: v3 adds capybara-7k preference-training data alongside dpo-mix-7k for the retained LLM alignment task. TLA, Hopper, and AlpacaEval remain; no new language or application domain is documented. The noise level 0.2 results already existed in v2 and are relocated to v3's appendix.

E2.justification: The LLM comparison changes from SLiC-HF, ORPO, and CPO to ORPO, CPO, DPO, and SimPO; SLiC-HF remains in MuJoCo comparisons. v3 also adds a static SFT+SimPO control and evaluates KTO and Jensen-Shannon f-DPO in the TLA base/noisy comparisons in Table 5. These substantially broaden the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: LLM training changes from three to four epochs, beta from 0.5 to 0.05, and the judge from Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct to Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct. v3 adds Mistral-7B and specifies three SFT epochs followed by one lower-learning-rate PO epoch for DPO/SimPO. For TLA, SimPO is newly listed under the 10-SFT-plus-2-PO-epoch protocol, despite retaining a contradictory no-SFT description. This establishes a reported setting revision, not evidence of rerunning unchanged scores.

E4.justification: v3 adds temporal-schedule comparisons, an LLM gamma sweep, a static SFT+SimPO control, and qualitative tests of directly transferring discovered objectives. These investigate temporal weighting, continued optimization, and transfer failures. v2's CoLPO/ORPO final-batch log-probability diagnostic is removed. Existing MuJoCo noise, gradient, Hopper, and bad-judge analyses are retained.

E5.justification: MuJoCo still reports means and standard errors over 25 trained agents, and the main LLM comparisons retain standard errors. However, v3's new ablation Table 3 supplies only win-rate and length-controlled win-rate point estimates despite its caption promising standard errors, introducing a limited gap in uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2's LLM table, including CoLPO's 31.94 win rate and 24.01 length-controlled win rate, is replaced by three configurations. v3's TA-MPO (3) reports win rates of 35.4, 39.4, and 41.6; DPO exceeds its length-controlled score on Gemma/dpo-mix, 31.0 versus 29.1. These are changed-method/protocol results, not same-setting gains. TA-MPO, KTO, f-DPO, and ablation entries are added, while matched original TLA and Hopper scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 adds a surrogate-classification formulation and minimizer argument in Appendix D and a derivation relating Bregman and f-divergence algorithm families in Appendix E. It also restores beta factors in Theorem 3.1 and the KKT derivation. The restated Theorem C.1 still omits those factors, leaving an internal inconsistency.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion replace the central CoLPO contribution—controlling chosen-response probability while continuing preference optimization—with TA-MPO's gradual transition from SFT to PO and its claimed alignment benefits. The broader claims about automatic objective discovery and MuJoCo performance are largely retained.

C2.justification: v3 replaces CoLPO's threshold-based mechanism explanation with an account emphasizing temporal weighting. Section 5 newly explains poor direct transfer of static discovered objectives through TLA overfitting, sparse LLM coverage, and extrapolation beyond training logits. Appendix E further attributes improvements primarily to changing g rather than divergence geometry. These materially qualify transferability and reinterpret the source of gains.

D1.justification: v3 adds an implementation link in Section 4 and discloses use of four NVIDIA L40S GPUs in Appendices K–L. It revises LLM training instructions and removes the standalone MuJoCo lambda=0.5 entry. Existing network, ES, software-library, batching, and LoRA details are largely retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds the KTO citation and removes the Gemma technical-report reference, supplying a model link instead. Previously cited Tang et al. and Wang et al. now support expanded discussion of classification-based reward modeling and Bregman versus f-divergences in Appendices D–E. The original related-work discussion remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the overall section sequence are retained. Targeted revisions rewrite the LLM-transfer discussion and conclusion, introduce a temporal-awareness subsection, reorganize the MuJoCo and meta-learning appendices, and update author and funding information. The language changes are localized rather than pervasive.

P2.justification: v3 converts the main text and references from two columns to one, adds a data-generation diagram and an LLM ablation table, and redesigns the LLM comparison table around model/dataset combinations. The baseline-objective table moves to Appendix A, and TLA results are redistributed across main and appendix tables. Existing gradient plots are retained with revised numbering and a shorter caption.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's single LLM configuration and three one-step baselines, v3 provides broader DPO/SimPO comparisons, component controls, and explicit transfer-failure analysis, strengthening empirical support and transparency. Conflicting SimPO settings, missing ablation uncertainties, and inconsistent theorem restatements limit the net gain. The changed methods and protocols do not establish that TA-MPO improves on CoLPO under comparable conditions.
